sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: LlamaIndex is an open-source Python framework for connecting language models to your own data. It loads documents such as PDFs, APIs and SQL databases, indexes them, and lets you ask questions over them, which is the basis of RAG apps and data agents.
sixtySeconds.problem: Language models only know their training data. LlamaIndex gives you data connectors, indexes and query engines so an LLM can answer from your private documents without you building that plumbing yourself.
whoFor: Python developers building RAG or document Q&A apps
Teams connecting LLMs to internal data
Beginners who want a five-line start
Advanced users customising retrievers and reranking
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for a mature data framework with more than 300 integration packages for LLMs, embeddings and vector stores, from a high-level API down to fully customisable modules.
requirements: An LLM: OpenAI by default, or a local model through Ollama

overview: There are two ways to install it. llama-index is a starter package with the core and a selection of integrations. llama-index-core is the core alone, to which you add only the integration packages you need, such as llama-index-llms-ollama or llama-index-embeddings-huggingface.

Imports that include core (llama_index.core) come from the core package; others come from integrations. A typical flow loads files with SimpleDirectoryReader, builds a VectorStoreIndex and queries it.

The README notes that the company's main focus is now LlamaParse, its commercial document-parsing platform, while the open-source framework stays available. It also says the README is updated less often than the documentation. The framework is MIT licensed.

steps.title: Add the integrations you need
steps.body: For example OpenAI, Ollama and Hugging Face embeddings.
steps.code:
pip install llama-index-llms-openai
pip install llama-index-llms-ollama
pip install llama-index-embeddings-huggingface

environment.name: OPENAI_API_KEY
environment.description: Needed for the default OpenAI models; not needed with Ollama and local embeddings.

firstRun.title: Index a folder and build a vector index
firstRun.code:
from llama_index.core import VectorStoreIndex, SimpleDirectoryReader

documents = SimpleDirectoryReader("YOUR_DATA_DIRECTORY").load_data()
index = VectorStoreIndex.from_documents(documents)
